hints: The mex is the smallest missing nonnegative integer.
A window of k elements must have mex at most k.
Maintain frequencies for 0 through k and an ordered set of those currently missing.
analogy: There are k+1 candidate numbered seats and only k occupants, so at least one seat is empty.
example: For windows [0,1,1] and [1,1,3], the mex values are 2 and 0.
algorithm: Keep frequencies for values at most k and an ordered set initially containing 0 through k. Remove a value from the set when its frequency becomes positive; add it back when the frequency falls to zero. Ignore values above k. Output the smallest missing value for each complete window.
correctness: At least one of 0 through k is absent because there are only k elements. The set contains exactly the absent candidates, so its minimum is the mex.
complexity: For n elements and window size k, O(n log k) time and O(k) space.
